coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Decent Work Act 2015 covers domestic workers (min wage reported US$0.43/h or US$3.50/day; written statement and contract copy kept 5 years). NASSCORP is formal-sector oriented; sources conflict on rates (4-6% employer) and deadlines (10th vs 15th of next month); no evidence private households must register. MYNASSCORP app exists for contributions. Nothing usable found; weak.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Scrap business licences issued via Mines and Energy; Inter-Agency Scrap Regulator Committee chaired by MME; Liberia Scrap Dealers Association exists (New Dawn, 5 Mar 2024). A 2019 Ministry of Commerce regulation restricting scrap export is listed on liblaw.org (not opened). No fee, register or reporting detail found.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Liberian pawnbroker or second-hand goods regime found in the one combined search; MoT regulation covers used vehicle dealers only (see 5). Likely not applicable or informal.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K03 (gold dealers/brokers). No separate jewellery-buyer register found; no search spent.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: MoT administrative regulation covers new/used vehicle dealerships, motorcycles, auto spare parts stores and garages; requires eligibility certificate, zoning compliance, Liberian ownership for used-car dealers; used vehicles max 10 years old. MoT said it would inspect eligibility certificates. May 2025 MoT codified all administrative regulations. Eligibility-certificate docx could not be read (binary).

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: FAO job posting: a Veterinary and Animal Health Disease Law is being drafted, to regulate live animal markets and live bird markets. Not confirmed enacted. No permit or register detail found.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: MoA/FAO flag shortage of meat inspectors and slaughter facilities; MCC arrested roasted-meat traders for hygiene; US$4M Careysburg slaughterhouse announced in 2016. No butcher permit or register found.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No search spent; no beekeeper register or duty known in Liberia, and the sector is small and informal.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Standard Treatment Guidelines for veterinary services recommend limiting vet drugs to licensed veterinarians and pharmacies; no veterinary council or drug-shop licence found; new law being drafted (see 6). Unverified.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: No Liberian driller licence or abstraction permit found; water regulation fragmented between EPA, LHS, MPW and LWSC; most national water standards still draft (USAID profile 2021). Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: July 2026 MCC public-private partnership: 30 Liberian community-based enterprises and SMEs picked in phase 1; NACOBE coordinates CBEs, LISWA supervises private companies; CBEs pay annual fee to MCC and collect fees from households; non-payment is a problem. New MCC municipal regulations approved. No septic or faecal-sludge licensing found.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: No search spent; no Liberian pressure-equipment or lift inspection regime known, and the building stock is thin.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Sachet/bottled water producers hit by EPA closure order effective 20 Jan 2026 (Environmental Protection and Management Law s.35.1(a)(i)); see candidate. No community water system register found.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Liberia Plant Pesticide Regulatory Services Bureau Act exists (FAOLEX summary: registration, labelling, storage, marketing). No dealer licence, fees or register detail confirmed; MoA pest management plan under WAATP is a project document.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: No private recruitment agency licence regime found. Ministry of Labour directive of 17 June 2026: every new alien work permit application needs proof of 30-day advertising in local media (Decent Work Act 45.1(c)(i); Revised Regulation 17 of 2019).

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Public Health Law requires a permit to handle remains within 24 hours; funeral homes affiliated variously to MoH, EPA, NPHIL and a Liberia Funeral Home Association; Feb 2026 exhumation court case sparked debate on funeral home regulation. No licence regime found.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision

Churches not confirmed. Halal/kosher not applicable.

result.competitor: None found. Searches for an online EPA Liberia permit portal and for local compliance apps for water producers returned nothing Liberia-specific. Compliance is done manually through the EPA, NPHIL lab testing (alleged US$125), the EPA fee (alleged US$225), PCC (US$75 per machine) and LWSC (US$150).
result.duty: Under the Environmental Protection and Management Law s.35.1(a)(i), producers must register with the EPA and hold an operating permit. They must submit periodic water-quality results to accredited labs, and they also need NPHIL permits (Public Health Law). The penalty is immediate closure, enforced with police support; no fine amount was stated for water plants. EPA did fine China Union US$120k in 2024, which shows its fining power. The renewal cycle and testing frequency are not specified in the sources (unverified).
result.market: No current register was found. NPHIL inspected about 125 water producers in Monrovia and its environs in 2017 and closed 55. The 2026 EPA action named 11 firms plus "several others". The likely national total is somewhere in the low hundreds, an estimate I could not verify.
result.reason: The duty is real. Under the EPML s.35.1(a)(i), EPA closed unpermitted sachet and mineral water plants from 20 Jan 2026. Producers must hold an EPA operating permit and NPHIL permits and submit periodic lab tests. I found no Liberian software or online EPA portal for this. The pain is fees, hygiene and enforcement, not tracking. A plant deals with only a few permits and tests a year, which is easy to manage on paper. Owners are informal, have thin margins and are protesting the fees (LWPA shutdown threat), so they are unlikely to pay for software. The market is small: about 125 producers were inspected around Monrovia in 2017. Renewal frequency, the official fee schedule and how the dispute ended are unverified. A done-for-you compliance service through LWPA is more plausible than a SaaS product.
